title: Cardinal Numbers, Time & Dates
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 36; Ryding Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.4)
objectives: Apply chiastic gender polarity for cardinal numbers 3–10.
Inflect compound numbers 11–19 (invariable fatḥah, except 12) and decades 20–90.
Assign the correct case and number to the counted noun (tamyīz al-ʿadad).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 5: How do sound masculine plurals inflect across nominative, accusative, and genitive?

sections.heading: Gender Polarity & Counted-Noun Syntax
sections.body: Classical Arabic cardinal numbers follow two interlocking rules: (1) gender agreement (3–10 take the OPPOSITE gender of the singular counted noun) and (2) the case and number of the counted noun (tamyīz al-ʿadad), which shifts across number bands.

sections.label: The Three Counted-Noun Bands
sections.summary: 3–10: plural genitive (e.g., ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ, reverse gender). 11–99: singular accusative (e.g., أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا, عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا). 100 & 1000: singular genitive (e.g., مِائَةُ رَجُلٍ).

sections.arabic: قَرَأْتُ أَرْبَعَةَ كُتُبٍ فِي عِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا
sections.transliteration: qaraʾtu ʾarbaʿata kutubin fī ʿishrīna yawman
sections.translation: I read four books in twenty days.
sections.irab: أَرْبَعَةَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ (مُضَافٌ) | كُتُبٍ: مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ جَمْعٌ مَجْرُورٌ | عِشْرِينَ: مَجْرُورٌ بِاليَاءِ | يَوْمًا: تَمْيِيزٌ مُفْرَدٌ مَنْصُوبٌ
sections.notes: Because كِتَابٌ is masculine, 'four' takes feminine ة (أَرْبَعَةَ) + plural genitive كُتُبٍ. After عِشْرِينَ, يَوْمًا is singular accusative.

sections.heading: Always Check the Singular Gender for 3–10
sections.body: Determine gender polarity from the SINGULAR of the counted noun, not its plural (e.g., أَيَّامٌ 'days' has singular يَوْمٌ masc., so 'three days' is ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ).
